monthly_review.summary: You've reduced volume and intensity this month but improved pace consistency and aerobic training effect — a strategic shift toward quality over quantity.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 25.5 km less and 6 fewer sessions, your average pace improved by 25 sec/km and aerobic training effect rose from 2.7 to 3.0 — indicating higher-quality efforts.

goal_tracker.message: You need 25.5 more km across 6 remaining sessions — averaging 4.3 km per session — to match last month's volume. Prioritize one longer run (8–10 km) and four moderate runs (4–5 km) with at least two in Zone 2–3 HR.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose to 13.64 m/sec per bpm (from 13.46), even as avg HR increased +4 bpm — suggesting better cardiovascular economy during sub-threshold efforts, likely supported by the 14.1 km long run at only 141 bpm.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity distribution
insights.body: Zone 4 time jumped from 15% (June) to 23%, and Zone 5 appeared (10% vs 1%), while Z1–Z2 dropped from 53% to 41% — indicating a deliberate move toward threshold and VO2 max work, especially evident in the 10.0 km run at 166 bpm (Zone 4).

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence dropped to 136 spm on the 4.0 km recovery run (July 8), yet stride length increased to 85.3 cm — unusual for low-effort runs and possibly compensatory; contrast with the 14.1 km run where cadence held at 151 spm but stride shortened to 70.4 cm, reflecting form preservation under fatigue.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Three of five July runs (July 1, 5, 12) had aerobic TE ≥3.1, including back-to-back efforts (July 5 & 6) — yet no Z1-only recovery run appears in recent logs, potentially limiting autonomic recovery given rising avg HR (+4 bpm) and declining Z1/Z2 time.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on July 15, focusing on cadence ≥150 spm and relaxed arm swing — no pace target.
recommendations.reason: Your Z1–Z2 time dropped to 41% (vs 53% last month) and you have no true recovery run in the last 5 sessions; this restores parasympathetic balance and supports aerobic base resilience.

recommendations.action: Repeat the 10.0 km run from July 5 — but hold avg HR ≤162 bpm (upper Zone 4) and aim for cadence ≥153 spm throughout.
recommendations.reason: That run delivered 4.0 aerobic TE and 154 spm cadence at 166 bpm — lowering HR slightly while maintaining cadence will improve lactate clearance efficiency and reduce cardiac strain.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-sec strides (90% effort, full recovery) after your next easy run, focusing on quick turnover and minimal vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation dipped to 7.6 cm on July 8 (low HR run) but averaged 7.9–8.5 cm otherwise; neuromuscular priming can reinforce efficient form without added load.

weekly_focus.description: Balance high-quality efforts with purposeful physiological recovery — using heart rate control and cadence awareness to reinforce aerobic efficiency while maintaining intensity gains.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (45 min, HR ≤135 bpm)
Threshold tempo run (10 km, HR 160–162 bpm)
